notes.meaning: God calls His people to sing out with loud and joyful praise. He is named their strength because He rescued them from Egypt and gave them power to endure trials. Hearty, glad worship is what honors Him best.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that because Asaph means congregation, this call to praise is given to the baptized Church, who should rejoice aloud even when words fail.

notes.meaning: The people are urged to strike up music using hand drums, sweet harps, and lyres. These instruments brought great joy and accompanied sacred dancing during Israel's holy feasts. Joyful music helps God's people express the gladness of their hearts.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine allegorized the verse, viewing the psalm as spiritual truth and the drum of animal skin as material goods, teaching that believers who receive spiritual teaching should give physical support in return.

notes.meaning: The priests were told to blow the ram's horn to announce the sacred feast days. This horn signaled the start of a new month and the great festival times, like the Feast of Tabernacles. It summoned the whole nation to stop their work and gather for worship.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine took the New Moon as a symbol of new life in Christ, so blowing the horn represents boldly preaching that new life.

notes.meaning: These gatherings were not human inventions, but laws commanded directly by the God of Jacob. Because the Lord Himself appointed them, Israel had a sacred obligation to keep them faithfully. Gathering with God's people is a duty based on His holy word.

differ.view: Worship practices and holy days must have an explicit command in Scripture, meaning the church should not invent religious holidays like Christmas or Whitsun.

notes.meaning: God set up this testimony for the whole family of Israel, here called Joseph, when He went out against Egypt to deliver them. While enslaved there, the Israelites had lived under masters who spoke an unfamiliar foreign language. Deliverance brought them into direct fellowship with the Lord who spoke to them.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interpreted leaving Egypt as a picture of baptism, after which the believer begins to understand spiritual mysteries like a new and unfamiliar language.

notes.meaning: The Lord speaks directly, reminding His people how He freed them from harsh slavery in Egypt. Their shoulders were relieved from heavy burdens, and their hands were freed from carrying bricklayers' baskets. God's grace rescues those who are helpless to free themselves.

When Israel cried out in misery, God heard them and delivered them, answering from the cloudy thunder-pillar at the Red Sea. Later, He tested their trust at Meribah when they complained about water. God proves our faith in hard times so that we learn to rely fully on Him.

The Lord calls His people to quiet down and listen to His solemn covenant warning. He had already rescued them, and now He pleads with them to pay close attention to His voice. True worship always includes listening to what God commands.

God restates the first of the Ten Commandments, forbidding any strange or foreign god among them. Israel was never to worship the idols of the nations around them, nor let anything else replace the Lord in their hearts. Believers must give God their wholehearted devotion.

The Lord identifies Himself as the only true God, the One who brought Israel safely out of Egypt. He pictures them like hungry birds, inviting them to open their mouths wide in prayer and faith so He can satisfy them with good things. God stands ready to meet all the real needs of His people.

Despite all God had done, His people chose to shut their ears to His voice. They did not want His guidance, His laws, or His rule over their lives. Turning away from God's word is the root of all spiritual failure.

Because they were obstinate, God withdrew His restraining grace and handed them over to their own stubborn desires. When people repeatedly reject God, His most dreadful judgment is to let them follow their own foolish plans. Running our own way leads only to ruin.

The Lord speaks with deep, heartfelt sorrow over the disobedience of His people. He earnestly wishes that Israel would listen to Him and walk in the good paths He planned for them. God takes no pleasure in the ruin of sinners.

differ.view: God's wish expresses what He commands and approves in His law, not His eternal decree, since His sovereign purpose cannot be resisted.
God's grief shows His sincere desire for the salvation of all people, genuinely longing for them to turn and live rather than perish.

notes.meaning: If Israel had remained obedient, God would have quickly subdued all their enemies for them. Their struggles lingered on not because God lacked strength, but because their own sins kept His deliverance away. Unrepented sin leaves God's people open to attack.

Those who hated the Lord would have been forced to bow down before Him in pretended obedience. In contrast, the peace and prosperity of God's faithful people would have lasted forever. Walking with the Lord brings lasting safety.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine understood the lasting time to mean that the eternal doom and punishment of God's enemies would never end.

notes.meaning: God promised that faithful obedience would be rewarded with the richest wheat and sweet honey taken straight from rocky cliffs. He wanted to satisfy them completely with the best of all His blessings. Trusting God opens the door to His richest spiritual food.
